newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany postpones cut in solidarity tax - sources.
newsitem.headline: Germany postpones cut in solidarity tax - sources.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition decided on Friday to delay a planned cut in the solidarity surcharge on income tax, to help bridge a spending gap in 1997, government sources said.

The unpopular solidarity tax was to have been cut to 6.5 percent from the current 7.5 percent effective January 1. No decision had yet been reached on whether the petroleum tax would be increased, another revenue measure under consideration, the sources said.

Officials of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and their Free Democrat coalition partners were expected to announce details of the tax policy agreements starting at 1000 GMT, the sources said.
The spending gap, estimated at 10 billion marks, appeared this week due to decisions to allow a wealth tax to lapse and to raise the government's allowance for children.
Reports that the government was considering an increase in the petroleum tax sparked widespread protest from opposition parties, leading newspapers, business associations and taxpayer groups.
